title: Totem: Object-Centric 3D Memory for World-Consistent Video Generation
summary: Generating coherent videos grounded in a unified underlying world remains a major challenge, particularly under large viewpoint changes, where existing methods often struggle to maintain stable representations of individual objects. To this end, we introduce Totem, an object-centric 3D memory framework for world-consistent video generation. Totem first represents each selected object as a persistent 3D memory aligned to a shared world frame, assigning it a dedicated state. Based on these memories, we design a dual-stream 3D conditioning architecture that combines object memories with scene geometry for target-view synthesis. Moreover, these object memories constrain the model's attention with 3D structural information, thereby preserving object surfaces and relative spatial layouts. Extensive experiments on world-generation and object-centric benchmarks demonstrate that Totem generates videos depicting a more object-consistent 3D world under challenging camera trajectories, while supporting versatile applications.
tldr: Totem is an object-centric 3D memory framework that ensures world-consistent video generation by tracking objects as persistent 3D representations, enabling stable rendering across large viewpoint changes.
tldr_zh: Totem 是一个以对象为中心的 3D 记忆框架，通过将对象表示为持久的 3D 状态，实现了在大视角变化下视频生成的一致性和 3D 世界稳定性。

title: SurgCast: Action-Conditioned Future Skeletons for Controllable Surgical World Models
summary: Surgical world models must turn prospective robot actions into visually faithful, structurally consistent instrument motion. We introduce SurgCast, which predicts future instrument skeletons from current structure, robot state, and future actions, then uses the forecast to control video generation. Dual-path injection combines skeleton geometry with derived, instrument-specific motion descriptors through geometric residuals and conditioning modulation. Both paths complement native action conditioning and are retained in a four-step causal student. On SutureBot and SRTH-Porcine-Cholei, the teacher and student improve all seven reported quality and instrument-consistency metrics over their respective direct-action baselines; teacher FVD decreases by 37.6% and 67.3%. Ablations show that future actions improve skeleton prediction and that combining both injection paths performs best across all six metrics under predicted skeletons. These results support using predicted articulated structure and its motion semantics as a control interface for surgical video prediction. Project videos and examples are available at https://surgcast.netlify.app/.
tldr: SurgCast is a novel surgical world model that improves video generation by predicting future instrument skeletons based on robot actions and state, using a dual-path injection mechanism to enhance motion consistency.
tldr_zh: SurgCast 是一种新型手术世界模型，通过结合机器人动作与当前状态预测未来的手术器械骨架，并利用双路径注入机制提升视频生成的动作一致性。

title: A Plausible Future Is Not a Causal Future: Can Video Models Generate How the World Unfolds?
summary: Large-scale video generation models are increasingly viewed as a promising path toward world models, yet their ability to capture causally coherent physical dynamics remains poorly understood. Existing evaluations largely emphasize visual quality, prompt adherence, or broad physical plausibility, leaving open whether a model can faithfully realize a complete causal cascade, in which an initiating event propagates through causally dependent interactions to a terminal outcome. We introduce CausalCascade, a simulator-grounded benchmark centered on 50 event-rich Blender scenes with structured event graphs, graph-grounded diagnostic VQA, three levels of future-event specification, and 2,832 controlled counterfactual variants, and use it to evaluate nine image-to-video models with complementary motion-, event-, and counterfactual-level diagnostics. Across the evaluated models, generated motion is more reliably localized spatially than realized with correct spatiotemporal evolution, while richer future-event specification improves event recovery but leaves physical realization limited. Counterfactual evaluation further reveals weak selective responsiveness to physical interventions, while most audited failures are foundational, arising at scene consistency or event occurrence. Together, these results position causal cascade generation as a process-level test of world modeling and highlight the need to jointly recover the intended future, faithfully realize its physical evolution, selectively respond to physical interventions, and maintain a coherent physical world over time. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/SJTU-DeepDeltaLab/CausalCascade .
tldr: The paper introduces CausalCascade, a simulator-grounded benchmark designed to evaluate whether modern video generative models can faithfully simulate causal dynamics and physical interactions rather than just plausible-looking visual sequences.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了一个名为 CausalCascade 的模拟器驱动基准，旨在评估现代视频生成模型是否能够真实模拟因果动态和物理交互，而不仅仅是生成视觉上逼真的序列。

title: ELECT: Settling Identity Before Rendering for Scalable Story Visualization
summary: Training-free story visualization without reference images must preserve recurring entities across frames while scaling to long narratives. Existing methods typically maintain consistency by conditioning each frame on other frames of the same story, coupling generation time, VRAM, or both to story length. We introduce ELECT, which instead settles cross-frame identity before final rendering through a language-guided scene-entity mapping and stationary anchors elected from the model's own drafts. This makes the per-frame cost of the final rendering pass independent of story length. Joint attention exceeds 96 GB of VRAM at 32 scenes, whereas ELECT remains at 8.3 s per frame and under 20 GB VRAM from 10 to 1000 scenes. On the Story50 long-story benchmark, ELECT reaches 0.833 average Character Consistency Similarity (aCCS), compared with 0.826 for ten-round refinement, at one seventh of its generation cost, with lower text alignment (0.327 vs. 0.340). At 1000 scenes, to our knowledge, the first evaluation of training-free story visualization at this length, ELECT exceeds ten-round refinement by 0.017 aCCS and the nearest flat-cost baseline by 0.091, while also surpassing refinement in text alignment at one twenty-fourth of its generation time. These results show that long-horizon consistency need not require increasingly expensive inter-frame conditioning as stories grow.
tldr: ELECT introduces a novel identity-preservation framework for long-form story visualization that decouples cross-frame consistency from generation cost by settling entity representations before the final rendering pass.
tldr_zh: ELECT 提出了一种用于长篇故事可视化的新型身份保持框架，通过在最终渲染前预先确定实体表示，成功将跨帧一致性与生成成本解耦。

title: Structured Stateful Relational Scripts with a High-Quality Dataset for Multi-Shot Audio-Visual Video Generation
summary: Coherent multi-shot audio-visual video generation requires maintaining consistent identities while depicting evolving states and coordinating sounds across shot boundaries. Although dense captions describe individual shots in detail, they rarely specify which entities persist, how their states change, or which entities and actions produce sounds. To address this limitation, we propose Structured Stateful Relational Scripts (SSRS), a textual supervision representation that separates persistent entity and voice identities from shot-specific visual and auditory states. SSRS explicitly encodes sound-source bindings and temporal relations, while a global audio-visual event sequence connects local actions and sounds, including events that continue across shot boundaries. We further introduce MSAV-Script-100K, a large-scale dataset of curated multi-shot audio-visual videos paired with detailed SSRS annotations, enabling models to learn identity persistence, state transitions, and event continuity from structured supervision. Experiments demonstrate improvements in cross-shot consistency, adherence to specified state changes, and audio-visual alignment, highlighting the effectiveness of our SSRS and MSAV-Script-100K for coherent multi-shot audio-visual generation. Our proposed dataset is available at \href{https://huggingface.co/datasets/shenlehan/MSAV-Script-100K}{MSAV-Script-100K}.
tldr: The paper introduces Structured Stateful Relational Scripts (SSRS) and the MSAV-Script-100K dataset to improve identity consistency, state transitions, and audio-visual alignment in multi-shot video generation.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了结构化状态关系脚本（SSRS）和 MSAV-Script-100K 数据集，旨在解决多镜头视频生成中的身份一致性、状态转换及视听对齐问题。

title: EmoTrace-Bench: Diagnosing Emotional Expression in Text-to-Video Generation through Controlled Cues and Intensity
summary: Text-to-video (T2V) models are increasingly used to generate videos with targeted emotional expressions, yet existing evaluation methods mainly rely on holistic video-text alignment and provide limited insight into whether failures arise from target-emotion expression, intensity control, or specific affective cues. We introduce EmoTrace-Bench, a fine-grained diagnostic benchmark that controls emotion intensity and selected affective cues in prompts and evaluates generated videos at multiple levels. EmoTrace-Bench contains 448 controlled prompts covering eight emotions, two intensity levels, and diverse cue conditions. Using 12 T2V models, we generate 5,376 videos and evaluate target-emotion presence, perceived intensity, and ten audiovisual dimensions of emotional expression with an automated evaluator calibrated and validated against human annotations on a subset of the data. Results reveal substantial differences across models and prompt designs. Prompts that explicitly describe a character's emotional reaction are followed more reliably than prompts that describe only events or scenes, whereas adding more affective cues or using more explicit cinematic audiovisual language does not consistently improve emotional generation. These results illustrate how aggregate alignment scores may overlook localized differences in target-emotion expression, intensity control, and cue realization. EmoTrace-Bench provides a traceable and interpretable framework for diagnosing emotional video generation without modifying existing generation pipelines, and we release the prompts and the automated evaluation rules.
tldr: EmoTrace-Bench is a new diagnostic benchmark for text-to-video generation that evaluates emotional expression, intensity control, and affective cue realization using a fine-grained, automated framework.
tldr_zh: EmoTrace-Bench 是一个用于评估文生视频模型情感表达能力的基准测试，通过受控提示词和多维自动化评估指标，精准诊断模型在情感表现力、强度控制和情感线索应用上的局限性。

title: OmniRSI: Taming Latent Diffusion for Unified Multimodal Remote Sensing Image Generation
summary: Multimodal remote sensing image generation emerges as a promising paradigm for recovering complete and complementary observations from heterogeneous and partially observed remote sensing data. However, existing methods predominantly depend on sensor-specific fine-tuning of natural image generation models, limiting unified multimodal generation capacity due to the absence of shared representations and robust conditioning mechanisms. To address these challenges, we propose OmniRSI, a unified multimodal remote sensing image generation model. Specifically, we develop a remote sensing-specific variational autoencoder that captures multimodal priors and promotes a locally smooth latent space for unified representation and robust reconstruction across diverse observed data. Building upon that, we fully adapt Stable Diffusion 3.5 with a ControlNet branch to support unified multimodal generation and translation conditioned on textual and visual cues. Besides, we devise a training-free cyclic latent alignment mechanism that iteratively enriches incomplete visual conditions with generated multimodal information, progressively improving guidance reliability while preserving observed measurements. We also construct RSI-MM, a large-scale dataset comprising 11.5M multi-resolution images with text annotations and partially paired data for training and evaluation. Extensive experiments verify that OmniRSI achieves superior performance in multimodal reconstruction, generation and translation.
tldr: OmniRSI is a unified multimodal remote sensing image generation model that utilizes a custom VAE and a ControlNet-adapted Stable Diffusion 3.5 framework, supported by a large-scale multimodal dataset, RSI-MM.
tldr_zh: OmniRSI 是一个统一的多模态遥感图像生成模型，它利用定制的变分自编码器（VAE）和集成 ControlNet 的 Stable Diffusion 3.5 架构，并配套了名为 RSI-MM 的大规模遥感多模态数据集。

title: TempoKV: Predictive KV Cache Quantization for Autoregressive Video Generation
summary: Autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models enable streaming generation of long videos but suffer from significant memory overhead due to the rapidly growing KV cache. Existing KV cache quantization methods are primarily designed for LLMs and transfer poorly to video models, where activations exhibit different statistics and strong spatiotemporal redundancy. We observe that the video KV cache is largely predictable over time, with a clear asymmetry. Keys are highly predictable from their temporal history, while values depend primarily on the current key and need a short history of preceding values. Based on these observations, we propose \textbf{\method}, a training-free predictive KV cache quantization framework for AR video generation. \method predicts keys and values according to their distinct dependencies and stores only the residuals at low precision. Both predictors are lightweight, calibrated once offline by linear regression on a small set of BF16 samples, and remain fixed across prompts and generation runs. Experiments on Self-Forcing, Causal Forcing, and LongCat-Video-13B show that \method consistently achieves higher generation quality than existing KV cache quantization methods at comparable or higher compression ratios, reaching up to $6.71\times$ KV cache compression with the best overall quality--efficiency tradeoff. Our code will be released on GitHub.
tldr: TempoKV is a training-free KV cache quantization framework that exploits spatiotemporal redundancy in autoregressive video generation to achieve up to 6.71x compression by predicting keys and values and storing only residuals.
tldr_zh: TempoKV 提出了一种用于自回归视频生成的无需训练的 KV Cache 量化框架，通过利用视频的时空冗余性预测键值并仅存储残差，实现了高达 6.71 倍的压缩比。

title: HGA-Quant: Heterogeneity-Aware Quantization for AutoRegressive Visual Generation Models
summary: Recently, AutoRegressive Visual Generation (ARVG) models have emerged as a competitive paradigm for high-quality image synthesis. However, their substantial computational and memory demands make them difficult to deploy on resource-constrained edge devices. Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) provides a promising solution to reduce the computational and memory costs of ARVG models, yet existing methods often suffer from substantial image quality degradation under low-bit quantization. In this paper, we propose a training-free PTQ framework for ARVG, consisting of Tail-Aware Bounded-init Grid Refinement (T-BGR) and Coarse-to-Fine Activation Precision Scheduling (CAPS). T-BGR introduces a tail-aware reconstruction objective for weight quantizer calibration, assigning greater importance to distribution-tail coefficients and preserving fine-grained information without introducing additional parameters or high-precision branches. CAPS performs coarse-to-fine activation precision scheduling by jointly considering the importance and computational cost of different generation stages, enabling efficient mixed-precision allocation under a given bit budget. Extensive experiments on multiple ARVG backbones demonstrate that our framework consistently improves robustness under aggressive low-bit quantization. Notably, on Infinity, our framework achieves near full-precision image generation quality at an effective W4A5.6 activation precision, while existing methods at W4A6 still exhibit noticeable quality degradation or inconsistent performance. Code is available at https://github.com/lxm-lc/HGA-Quant.
tldr: HGA-Quant introduces a training-free PTQ framework for autoregressive visual generation models, utilizing tail-aware weight calibration and coarse-to-fine activation scheduling to achieve high-quality generation at aggressive low-bit precision.
tldr_zh: HGA-Quant 提出了一种针对自回归视觉生成模型的无训练量化框架，通过尾部感知权重校准和粗细结合的激活精度调度，在低比特下实现了高质量的图像生成。

title: TIDE: Trajectory-Informed Skill Distillation for Efficient Text-to-Video Prompt Optimization
summary: Text-to-video (T2V) models are highly sensitive to prompt specificity, while iterative prompt optimization typically improves generation quality only through repeated video generation and vision-language model evaluation at inference time. We propose TIDE, a framework that distills this costly search process into an interpretable and reusable prompt-rewriting Skill. TIDE formulates prompt rewriting as a set of source-conditioned rule modules, each targeting a distinct semantic dimension. Once distilled, the frozen Skill activates the relevant rules and generates both positive and negative prompts in a single LLM call, followed by only one T2V generation, without test-time visual search or backbone fine-tuning. Evolved using only 100 prompts over 14 hours, TIDE achieves prompt-optimization performance comparable to computationally expensive search-based methods. Moreover, when transferred to previously unseen video-generation models, TIDE outperforms existing approaches specifically designed or trained for those models. Code is available at https://github.com/xiningin/TIDE_T2V.
tldr: TIDE is a framework that distills iterative prompt-optimization processes into a lightweight, reusable 'skill' module, enabling high-quality video generation with a single LLM call and zero test-time visual feedback.
tldr_zh: TIDE 提出了一种将迭代式提示词优化过程蒸馏为可复用的“技能”模块的框架，实现了在单次 LLM 调用下完成提示词优化，无需测试时的视觉搜索或模型微调，即可提升视频生成质量。

title: UMAS3D: Unified Mask-Free 3D Editing with Region-Adaptive Source Preservation
summary: 3D editing aims to modify an existing 3D asset according to user intent while preserving geometry and appearance outside the intended edit region. Existing methods often rely on task-specific training, source-3D inversion, or external 3D masks, and lack a unified framework for diverse editing conditions and tasks. We propose UMAS3D, a unified 3D editing framework that is training-free, inversion-free, and free from external 3D masks. UMAS3D converts text, bounding boxes, reference images, and their combinations into common target-view guidance, after which addition, deletion, modification, appearance, and pose editing share the same downstream 3D generation process. Our key insight is to couple online edit-region estimation with region-aware source preservation. Mask-Free Adaptive Region Modeling (MARM) initializes an Edit/Keep prior from source-target visual differences and progressively refines it as the target structure evolves, while Source-Guided Preservation Steering (SGPS) constrains the current Keep-region states to retain source geometry and appearance without suppressing target-driven changes. Experiments show that UMAS3D supports addition, deletion, modification, appearance, and pose editing while effectively preserving unedited source content. These advances make UMAS3D a unified framework for flexible and source-preserving 3D editing across diverse editing conditions.
tldr: UMAS3D is a unified, training-free 3D editing framework that eliminates the need for manual masks or source inversion by using online region-adaptive modeling to balance new edits with source preservation.
tldr_zh: UMAS3D 是一个统一的、免训练的 3D 编辑框架，通过在线区域自适应建模在编辑需求与原始资产保留之间取得平衡，无需手动遮罩或繁琐的逆向工程。

title: TRIG: Toward Measuring Texture Realism in Image Generation
summary: This paper studies the backbone used by metrics for evaluating the quality of generated images. Although generative models have advanced rapidly, some outputs still exhibit unrealistic texture characteristics, and these differences are difficult to measure. Widely used evaluation metrics provide limited insight into texture realism, since they often rely on a backbone trained for another objective, such as image classification or image-text alignment. Such objectives typically encourage invariance to low-level variations that carry texture, so the resulting features primarily encode semantic and global structure. As a result, texture-specific discrepancies may not be explicitly captured. We propose TRIG, a metric directed at the texture realism of generated images. Its backbone is instead the discriminator of a generative adversarial network pre-trained on a texture dataset, which provides a learned prior for the local statistics of natural textures. A plausibility head is fine-tuned to identify local texture degradations, while preserving natural defocus and sensor noise as positive cases. On the features of this backbone, we compute a standard distributional distance between a reference set of real images and a set of generated ones. We apply TRIG to several generative models and observe closer agreement with human realness ratings than baseline metrics.
tldr: The paper introduces TRIG, a novel evaluation metric for generative models that focuses specifically on texture realism by utilizing a texture-focused GAN discriminator backbone rather than standard semantic-heavy classification backbones.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了一种名为TRIG的生成图像纹理真实性评估指标，通过采用预训练的GAN判别器作为骨干网络，解决了传统指标在捕捉局部纹理细节上的不足。

title: UniForge3D: Joint 3D Reconstruction and Generation in a Shared Anchor-Guided Space
summary: Generating complete 3D assets from sparse, unposed images requires preserving observed geometry while completing unseen regions. Joint reconstruction and generation offers a way to address both goals: reconstruction recovers the geometry observed in the input images, while generation contributes learned shape priors. However, combining camera-relative reconstruction with canonical-space generation introduces a coordinate mismatch that makes direct geometric interaction more difficult. Moreover, conditioning each 3D location on all views without accounting for their relevance may mix useful geometric evidence with unrelated image content, hindering local detail recovery. We present UniForge3D, which jointly models reconstruction and generation in a shared anchor-guided space, resolving their coordinate mismatch. This space follows the anchor view's azimuth while keeping the object upright. The two branches exchange features bidirectionally to predict per-view point maps and a complete sparse voxel structure. We further condition point-map prediction on the generated structure to establish pixel-to-voxel correspondences and select the most informative input view for each voxel. Features from the selected views then guide detailed shape generation, helping preserve observed geometric details. Our method achieves state-of-the-art appearance and geometry results on Toys4K and GSO, generating complete 3D assets with improved fidelity. Project webpage: https://xishuxishu.github.io/uniforge3d-project/
tldr: UniForge3D introduces a unified anchor-guided space to jointly perform 3D reconstruction and generation, using pixel-to-voxel correspondences to enhance geometric fidelity from sparse input views.
tldr_zh: UniForge3D 提出了一种共享的锚点引导空间，用于联合执行三维重建与生成，并通过像素到体素的对应关系增强了从稀疏输入视图中提取几何细节的能力。

title: Channel Match: Calibrating Shape Latents for Few-Step 3D Generation
summary: Recent native 3D generators achieve high-quality asset creation by modeling structured 3D latents with flow-based transformers, but their high-resolution generation remains computationally expensive due to costly iterative sampling. In this work, we introduce a few-step distillation framework for native 3D generation, enabled by continuous self-consistency training with a custom JVP FlashAttention kernel and an analytic velocity regression objective for sparse structured 3D latents. To stabilize joint optimization, we further introduce an adaptive loss weighting strategy that automatically balances them without manual tuning. Beyond acceleration, we reveal a previously overlooked failure mode of few-step native 3D generation: sampling-induced latent distribution drift preserves geometric correctness but disrupts downstream PBR texture synthesis, causing texture artifacts on geometrically valid assets. To address this issue, we propose Channel Match, a training-free adaptive per-channel latent calibration method that restores the latent distribution without modifying either generator. We validate our approach on TRELLIS.2 at the $1024^3$ resolution setting. Our two-step model achieves $4.5\times$ faster geometry sampling while maintaining geometry quality comparable to the many-step teacher, and Channel Match further improves rendering quality by recovering the latent interface between geometry and appearance generation.
tldr: Channel Match enables fast, few-step 3D generation by introducing a distillation framework for flow-based transformers and a latent calibration technique to prevent texture artifacts.
tldr_zh: Channel Match 提出了一种针对原生 3D 生成的少步蒸馏框架，并引入了潜在空间校准技术，在提升采样速度的同时解决了纹理质量下降的问题。

title: Generative Quantum Machine Learning Methods for Cancer Detection using Augmented Datasets
summary: Cancer detection using AI methods and image databases faces several challenges, including limited and imbalanced image datasets, long algorithm training times, and high-complexity feature generation. In particular, many cancer image datasets contain very few malignant examples compared to benign ones, limiting the amount of minority-class data available for training. Although classical AI and especially deep learning methods have had some success in providing cancer diagnostics, Quantum Machine Learning (QML) methods may offer advantages through high-dimensional feature representations, generative data augmentation, and the exploitation of feature correlations through quantum properties such as entanglement. In this paper, we propose using a generative QML method on the compressed breast ultrasound image dataset (BUSI) to generate synthetic images and hence augmented datasets for classifier training. In particular, we train a convolutional neural network with real, synthetic, and a combination of real and synthetic images. We test the algorithm on real images and provide comparative results for all three training cases. Our results show that the classifier trained entirely on synthetic images achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.802 (80.2%), compared with 0.760 (76.0%) for the real-data baseline.
tldr: This paper proposes a generative Quantum Machine Learning (QML) approach to address class imbalance in cancer ultrasound datasets, demonstrating that a classifier trained on synthetic QML-generated images can outperform those trained on real-data baselines.
tldr_zh: 本文提出了一种用于癌症超声影像检测的生成式量子机器学习（QML）方法，通过生成合成数据解决样本不平衡问题，实验结果显示使用合成数据训练的分类器性能优于仅使用真实数据的基准模型。

title: Co-DSL: Human-LLM Co-design of Reusable Spatial Concepts for Layout Generation
summary: We present Co-DSL, a framework in which users and LLMs co-design reusable spatial concepts for layout generation. In the first stage, our system allows users to create a library of personalized operations. To add a concept, a user provides a description, which the LLM converts into an initial implementation. The user can then observe the concept's execution behavior over example scenarios and provide lightweight feedback to the LLM, which revises the concept's implementation logic. In the second stage, given a library, an LLM can author a layout program that meets a new layout request from a user. Executing a layout program instantiates a concept-graph, a declarative composition of library concepts. In this way, we require the LLM only to specify which concepts should hold, while we use a solver to search for a layout that satisfies them. Across five spatial layout domains, we find that Co-DSL libraries let LLMs capture layout patterns that are challenging for prior fixed-operation systems, and demonstrate that our concept-graph representation is needed for LLMs to reliably compose concepts together. We further find that Co-DSL lets LLMs author generative layout programs that expose high-level parametric controls users can manipulate to explore a distribution of related layouts without re-prompting.
tldr: Co-DSL is a human-LLM co-design framework that uses a library of reusable spatial concepts and a solver-based concept-graph representation to generate layouts with high control and reliability.
tldr_zh: Co-DSL 是一个人机协作框架，通过让人类与大模型共同设计可复用的空间概念库，结合求解器辅助生成可控、可靠且具有参数化调整能力的布局。
